title: UABB Exhibit
subtitle: Urban research and exhibition model study for Shenzhen's everyday spatial systems
overview: UABB Exhibit collects an architecture-school research project around Shenzhen's urban texture, informal economies, public interfaces and exhibition storytelling. The model is presented as a spatial archive: a way to turn observation, mapping, drawing and physical assembly into a readable exhibit rather than a single finished building proposal.
storyHtml:
This work sits between urban research and exhibition design. It begins from observation: dense commercial streets, improvised thresholds, shopfront rhythms, service spaces and the layered public life that makes Shenzhen feel fast, practical and constantly rewritten.

The project translates those findings into an exhibit object. Instead of treating the city as a distant plan, the model compresses fragments of street life into a field that can be read up close. Scale, repetition and sectional cuts become tools for showing how ordinary urban systems produce atmosphere.

In SPACE, UABB Exhibit is treated as a study in representation. It is less about a single architectural answer and more about how research can become spatial: how PDFs, field notes, mappings and models can form an exhibition language for a city that resists simple summary.

The current desktop exhibit prioritizes the model as a primary artifact. Additional boards, captions and research material can be layered later once the installation has its own dedicated room.
